newsitem.title: JAPAN: WTO says Japan liquor tax against its rules - source.
newsitem.headline: WTO says Japan liquor tax against its rules - source.

text.p: Japanese government sources said on Thursday that an appellate panel of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) had ruled in a final report that Japan's liquor taxation system runs counter to the international trade body's rules.

But the government sources did not comment on whether Japan would change its liquor taxes after the WTO's final ruling. But Finance Ministry officials have said in recent months that if the WTO's final ruling fails to support Japan's claims, Japan's liquor taxes may need to be revised.

Japan appealed to the WTO to reconsider its initial finding after a WTO panel in Geneva found in July that the Japanese system of liquor taxes treated imported spirits such as whiskey and brandy unfairly, to the advantage of domestic products. A complaint on Japanese liquor taxes had been filed with the WTO by the European Union, backed by Canada and the United States.

The EU has said that Japan taxes imported spirits at rates more than six times those imposed on popular home products called shochu. Tokyo has argued that shochu -- a potent, colourless liquor made from barley -- is basically a beverage for poorer people, while whiskey and other imported spirits are drunk by more affluent consumers.
Some Japanese shares were affected by media reports that the WTO had made its final ruling.
Shares in Takara Shuzo Co Ltd fell in Tokyo afternoon trade on Thursday, depressed by the media reports. They ended down 70 yen at 1,050 in turnover of 2.768 million shares.

Kyodo news agency quoted Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama as telling reporters on Thursday that the government had not been formally informed of a result, but added that it was aware that the WTO was coming closer toward a final ruling.
